record.summary: Kavya Reddy, a freelance interior designer, verbally agreed in July with restaurateur Naveen Bhatt to design his new restaurant for a total fee of Rs.3,00,000, with 50% payable upfront. She started work, created concept drawings, a material palette, a 3D walkthrough, and attended three site meetings. Naveen paid Rs.50,000 as an advance in August, then stopped responding. In August he asked for an invoice for the balance. After about four months, Naveen said the project was on hold and that he had only agreed to a small fee for initial ideas. Kavya sent a draft invoice for Rs.3,00,000 in November; Naveen replied that it was more than discussed. Meanwhile, another contractor began building the restaurant using her layout, posting photos that resemble her designs. Kavya seeks to recover the unpaid fee and compensation for the unauthorized use of her designs, despite having no written contract or fee proposal.
record.goal: Recover the unpaid balance of Rs.2,50,000 and obtain compensation for the unauthorized use of her design work.
questions: Do you have the exact dates (day and month) of the three site meetings?
Can you provide the dates (or at least month and year) of the email exchanges where Naveen approved the layout?
Do you have any written acknowledgment from Naveen that the designs would be his exclusive property or that you would retain any rights?
Has Naveen or the other contractor responded to any formal demand or notice you may have sent regarding payment and use of the designs?
Do you have any documentation (e.g., screenshots) of the social media posts that show the other contractor's work resembling your designs?
contradictions: Naveen claims the work product is not usable and that the advance payment settled everything, while his email reply "love the layout, proceed with the lighting plan" indicates acceptance and reliance on the designs.
Naveen says he never agreed to the full fee, yet the WhatsApp message in August asked for an invoice for the balance, implying an expectation of further payment.
evidence: Bank record showing a Rs.50,000 payment from Naveen's business account with the narration "design advance."
Email attachments of concept drawings sent to Naveen, with his replies such as "love the layout, proceed with the lighting plan."
WhatsApp message from Naveen in August saying "send me the invoice for the balance whenever ready."
Calendar entries showing three site meetings; a photo from one meeting showing Kavya presenting the drawings to Naveen and his manager.
Draft invoice for Rs.3,00,000 sent in November, with Naveen's reply "this is more than we discussed."
Photos posted by another contractor on social media that display a layout resembling Kavya's drawings.

follow_up.question: When and where did you last see or use the missing item?
follow_up.why: This narrows the time and place to check for records or witnesses.

evidence_plan.heading: Scene and evidence review
evidence_plan.safety: Get to safety and seek medical or police help if needed. Do not enter or alter a scene to gather evidence. Leave physical collection to the authorities.
prompts: Where did each event happen, and what was the last confirmed time before it?
What did you actually see or hear? Where were you, and what could you see from there?
What was already different when you arrived, and what changed afterward? Say if you are unsure.

suggestions.title: Item identification and last known location
suggestions.look_for: Look for a serial number, receipt, older photo or repair record. Write down when and where you last saw the item and when you noticed it missing.
suggestions.why: This can establish which item is missing and narrow the time window. It cannot identify who took it by itself.
suggestions.action: Save copies of records you own. If a device location service shows a location, share it with police instead of going there yourself.

suggestions.title: Footage from an authorised keeper
suggestions.look_for: If cameras cover the relevant place, note their owner and the narrow time window from your timeline.
suggestions.why: It may show movement or timing. A camera can have blind spots or an inaccurate clock.
suggestions.action: Ask the owner or investigating officer to preserve the original recording promptly. Record your request. Use only footage you are authorised to access.

suggestions.title: Product, order and batch
suggestions.look_for: If available, note the seller, order ID, product name, batch, date on the packaging and when it was opened or served.
suggestions.why: These details can distinguish the particular product from a general complaint about a shop or brand.
suggestions.action: Retain copies of your order and any photos you already took. Do not taste or handle suspect food for evidence. Ask the food safety authority about any sample.

suggestions.title: Symptoms and timing
suggestions.look_for: Write down when you ate, when symptoms started, and whether anyone else independently reported symptoms. Keep any relevant treatment records.
suggestions.why: Timing can guide inquiries. It does not by itself establish what caused the illness.
suggestions.action: Seek medical care when needed. Report factual details and let qualified authorities handle formal sampling or testing.

suggestions.title: Possession, title and notices
suggestions.look_for: Gather records you already hold, such as agreements, deeds, orders, rent payments or notices. Note who occupied the property and when that changed.
suggestions.why: Documents and the timeline can help distinguish possession from a claim about legal ownership.
suggestions.action: Keep full copies and record where each came from. Request records through the issuing office or a lawyer when needed.

suggestions.title: Location and visible changes
suggestions.look_for: Note the address or boundary reference and any changed lock, barrier or damage you actually observed.
suggestions.why: This helps identify the location and the particular change in dispute.
suggestions.action: Document only from an area you may safely and lawfully access. Do not enter disputed space or confront anyone.

suggestions.title: Original records and an evidence log
suggestions.look_for: Keep records you lawfully have, with their surrounding context. For each item note the related event, who provided it, when you received it, and any transfer.
suggestions.why: The log distinguishes what you observed from what someone later told you and makes it easier to check the source.
suggestions.action: Keep an unchanged original and label working copies. Avoid editing originals, guessing gaps, or sharing evidence publicly.
